title: Auditor-Ready Transcript Generator for Data Residency & Retention Controls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Build an automated "auditor transcript" export that compiles a chronological, tamper-evident bundle of artifacts demonstrating our data residency and retention controls for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audits. The transcript must include control-to-artifact mapping, signed checksums, retention metadata, redaction handling for PII, and a small human-readable executive summary that auditors can consume without needing to open raw logs. This ticket focuses on product/PM scope: acceptance criteria, UX flows for generating the bundle from the Console, export formats, and the auditor UX. Engineering tickets will implement collectors and signing.

Goal: reduce auditor time-to-evidence and decrease support overhead by enabling customers and auditors to download a validated bundle that proves control adherence for a selected time range and jurisdiction.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: 'Generate Auditor Transcript' action available on Compliance -> Evidence exports for customers with required permissions
Export formats: ZIP with manifest.json + signed SHA256 checksums, and a human-readable PDF summary (A4) that maps exported files to SOC2/ISO control IDs
Control mapping: each artifact in the bundle must be annotated with mapped control IDs (SOC2 CC/ISO A) and timestamps covering the requested date range
Cryptographic signing: bundle manifest must be signed using customer-specific KMS key where available; otherwise signed with Redwood audit key and labeled accordingly
Tamper evidence: signing and checksums validate when re-imported; UI shows validation status
PII redaction: default export redacts user identifiers according to customer's redaction policy; customers can request a full unredacted bundle via an attested support workflow
Cross-region awareness: when the selected date range includes events from multiple regions, the manifest must indicate region-of-origin for each artifact and include residency assertions
Retention metadata: each artifact entry must include retention policy name, created_at, retention_expiry and legal_hold flag if present
Auditor checklist: generated PDF includes a one-page checklist linking artifacts to control statements and an index of evidence file names
Sample audit pass: internal audit team can successfully perform a mock auditor review with the generated bundle (sign-off by Security and Legal)
CLI parity: audit engineers can generate the same bundle via CLI with the same flags as Console

risks: Large exports could incur high egress/storage costs and slow down Console responsiveness
Customers with strict data residency may not allow KMS signing outside region unless private deployment configured
Potential for accidental PII leakage if redaction policies are not exhaustively tested
Auditors may request raw logs beyond what collectors currently retain; could require retention policy changes
